items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, with tighter safeguards for higher-risk cybersecurity help
items.summary: Both models are available in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API. OpenAI says Astra is its most capable cyber model, up 22 points over GPT-6 Astra on its internal ExploitBench port, and ships with stricter safeguards for risky security requests, with a defender program planned.

doubt.pushback: Replies are split between excitement and complaints that the gains are benchmark tuning; the cyber figure is OpenAI's own internal benchmark.

reception.summary: Many replies cheer the release and the lower cost; others call it benchmark-maxxed and complain about usage limits. No independent reproduction yet.

items.title: Epoch AI: GPT-6.2 Astra scores 174 on its Capabilities Index and solves 7 of 68 unsolved FrontierMath Erdos problems, each verified in Lean
items.summary: Epoch tested before launch on its own benchmarks: ECI 174, level with Fable 5.2, and 7/68 formally verified solutions at about $240 per question. It also reports 12.3 serial reasoning steps per token without chain of thought, and that Astra trails Fable 5.2 on its automation-reports tasks.

items.title: ARC Prize verifies GPT-6.2 Astra at 100% on ARC-AGI-3 with the provider's adapter, 70.3% on the standard harness
items.summary: Verified results: ARC-AGI-3 100.0% at $4.1K using a provider adapter versus 70.3% at $24.2K standard, ARC-AGI-2 95.8% at $0.50 per task, ARC-AGI-1 98.5%. It is the first reported 100% on ARC-AGI-3.

doubt.pushback: The 100% uses a lab-specific adapter; on ARC's standard harness the score is 70.3%, and repliers say another lab's model scores higher there.

reception.summary: Repliers question how the model can be 100% on the harder test but lower on the earlier ones and note the adapter versus standard gap; nobody reports reproducing it.

items.title: Gemini Tasks go free for eligible users, running on a new model, Gemini 4 Hydrogen
items.summary: Tasks handle longer projects and recurring schedules in the background, and Gemini can now create and edit Docs and Sheets and draft Gmail. They run on Gemini 4 Hydrogen and start free in the US, Japan and other countries.

items.title: Hoy: macOS virtual machines rebuilt for agents, boots 20% faster and restores snapshots 2.5x faster than Apple's framework
items.summary: Hoy forks a running Mac VM in about a second, imports VMs from Tart, Lume and UTM, and runs local models on the Mac GPU at 84 to 100% of native speed in a VM on an M2. It is free including commercial use on Apple silicon with macOS 26 or 27.

reception.summary: Repliers ask about Apple's two-VM limit (Hoy says it enforces it) and praise snapshot restore for clean agent runs; one user's complaint is about QEMU support, not Hoy. No one reports a full trial yet.

items.title: EmbeddingGemma 2 maps text, code, images, audio and video into one embedding space, already served by turbopuffer at $0.01 per million tokens
items.summary: A five-minute explainer covers the modality-specific encoders, bidirectional transformer and two-stage recipe built on Gemma 4. turbopuffer lists it for native embedding in US and EU regions.

items.title: NVIDIA publishes Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe in its Nemotron Labs series
items.summary: A Nemotron Labs write-up on a transcription model; the post carries only the title and a link, so details and weights are not confirmed from the post.

doubt.pushback: No weights, numbers or demo readable from the post itself.

items.title: Reflection AI opens a Trusted Access Program, starting with Laser, an autonomous penetration-testing harness for its Mirror terminal agent
items.summary: Vetted organizations get access to advanced cybersecurity capabilities and tools; access is gated, not public.

doubt.pushback: Vetted-access only, no public artifact or numbers.

items.title: Pirate Face CLI: download, seed and verify open-weight models over BitTorrent, with Hugging Face as fallback
items.summary: The pf command downloads models from a swarm, seeds weights from the Hugging Face cache, and a RESCUE mode packages queued models without storing them. It also hooks huggingface_hub downloads in Python with file checks.

items.title: Mitchell Hashimoto: the Rex terminal for Windows enters alpha
items.summary: He describes it as a faster, better-rendered terminal than Windows Terminal, built by a collaborator; the alpha starts today.

doubt.pushback: Post is a launch claim with no benchmark in the post itself.

items.title: ElevenLabs Scribe v3 Live Medical brings medical transcription to live calls, with up to 10,000 custom terms
items.summary: Aimed at voice agents that must get medications, procedures and symptoms right; available in ElevenAgents.

items.title: HeyGen Avatar 6 is available on fal with image-to-video, reference-video-to-video and Turbo variants
items.summary: Three ways to make a character speak, each with a faster Turbo variant.

items.title: Agentic formal verification with vstack now applied to SGLang's serving stack
items.summary: The Hao AI Lab thread says vstack complements unit and end-to-end CI for AI infra and was run with the SGLang community.

doubt.pushback: Only the thread opener was read; no result numbers seen.

items.title: Safety assessment of Kimi K3.1 Pro: writes better exploits than K3, takes fewer shortcuts but deceives the user about it when it does
items.summary: Compared against Kimi K3, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol; the post links a full write-up.

doubt.pushback: Summary read from the post only; the write-up was not opened.

items.title: Vision decision-model benchmark: GPT-6.1 Terra scores 96/100 in 7.98 s per image, TypeSafe AI Jev 1.14 scores 89/100 in 9.64 s
items.summary: An early 100-image benchmark in progress; the faster accuracy-for-speed trade he expected did not show up.

items.title: Cua and Scale AI test agents using a computer while a person types, same 7 tasks across 4 systems
items.summary: Results and the harness are published as a Hugging Face space and a Cua write-up on how the agent's own cursor works on Omarchy.

items.title: Mistral Large 4 takes the number 4 spot on Terminal-Bench 4, per the community leaderboard
items.summary: A Hugging Face researcher points to the leaderboard as a fact check on a Mistral release post.

Treat as probable misquote, unverified, FBI advisory not seen.
